title: Progressive dehydration: SDK patterns for offline streaming and tool delegation (PRD draft)
summary: This doc proposes a set of SDK patterns and a lightweight wire protocol for 'progressive dehydration' — trimming and checkpointing streaming sessions so clients (especially mobile and offline-first) can pause, transmit, or store compact session artifacts and later rehydrate them with minimal roundtrips. The goal is to enable partial streaming + tool-calling experiences that survive disconnects and bandwidth constraints while preserving structured output correctness and tool-safety guarantees.
background: Many customers embed hosted streaming calls in mobile or intermittently connected environments. Current session snapshots are either too heavy (full transcript + attachments) or too lossy (only last tokens). We need an approach that 1) produces compact resumable checkpoints during streaming, 2) preserves enough state to replay or continue tool calls deterministically where possible, and 3) offers clear SDK ergonomics so integrators can opt-in without complex server-side changes.
goals: Define an SDK-first API for creating compact streaming checkpoints (dehydrated snapshots).
Specify a minimal server-client handshake for rehydration that works across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
Preserve structured output invariants for partial results (JSON fragments, tool-call intents) so downstream clients can safely render and act on them.
Provide prefetch/hint primitives so clients can proactively fetch heavyweight artifacts (attachments, tool results) while offline.
Keep added latency during normal streaming negligible (dehydration should be incremental and async).
non_goals: Not building a full offline sync engine for large attachments; attachments are referenced via pointers and optionally pre-fetched.
Not changing model behaviour or internal KV-caching semantics — dehydration operates on observable session state.
Not requiring customers to modify tool implementations in most cases; we aim for tokenized/ephemeral tokens for delegation instead.
user_stories: Mobile chat: app streams a long assistant response, user loses connectivity mid-stream, app saves a compact checkpoint; when online, app resumes from the checkpoint and receives remaining tokens without re-running the whole request.

Field worker: collects images and form data offline, SDK records tool-call intents and lightweight object pointers; when network is available, SDK rehydrates and materializes tool results using prefetch hints.
Web progressive load: client renders first useful JSON fragment from structured output and hydrates other fields lazily as attachments arrive.
Enterprise: on Private deployment, infra team wants deterministic auditability — dehydrated artifacts include checksums and signed meta so replays are auditable.
key_design_principles: Incremental checkpoints are cheap: generate diffs / pointers rather than full transcripts frequently.
Separation of concerns: transcript + lightweight metadata (session pointers, tool intents) vs heavy payloads (attachments, tool binary blobs).
Backward-compatible: server accepts dehydrated snapshot metadata and can resume where feasible, otherwise falls back to graceful restart with clear SDK-level signals.
Safety-first for tool calls: any delegated tool invocation in a dehydrated snapshot must carry a short-lived capability token and a minimal replay-proof fingerprint.
Observability: every dehydration/rehydration action emits traceable events for cost, latency, and error analysis.
protocol_overview_steps: During streaming, SDK emits periodic 'checkpoint' events to hosted API: small JSON describing last-committed token index, active tool intents, and pointer list for attachments.
Server acknowledges with a checkpoint_id and optional server-side hints (e.g., precompute fallback summary or compacted KV slice).
Client persists the checkpoint (locally or remote storage) and may reference attachments by short-urls or object ids.

To resume: client sends checkpoint_id (or full snapshot) plus rehydrate_hint header; server verifies checksum and either resumes token generation from saved state or instructs client to fallback to a deterministic restart path.
Tool delegation: if a tool call was partially executed when checkpointed, server returns tool-call-status (pending/completed/failed) and an ephemeral capability for post-resume finalization.
sdk_ergonomics_and_api_sketches: Start call: client.startStream({sessionId, resumePolicy: 'dehydrate-every-5s' | 'on-event'}) returns stream handle.
Resume API: client.resumeStream({checkpointId, rehydrateStrategy: 'lazy'|'eager'}) returns stream that emits 'rehydrated' event then continues tokens.
Prefetch helpers: sdk.prefetchAttachments(['ptr']) returns promise that resolves when heavy payloads are available locally; prefetch can run while offline using cached tokens.
Tool surfaces: sdk.delegateToolCall(toolName, args, {capabilityStore: ephemeral}) returns an idempotent token and records expected structured-output contract for later reconciliation.
Events: 'checkpoint-saved', 'rehydration-start', 'rehydration-complete', 'rehydration-fallback', 'tool-delegation-expired' emitted to client for telemetry and UX.
structured_output_and_tool_semantics: Canonical fragments: streaming structured outputs (JSON objects) should be emitted as stable fragments with explicit fragment ids so checkpoints can reference them without ambiguity.

Tool-call placeholders: when a tool call is requested the stream emits a placeholder frame {tool_intent: {...}, placeholder_id}. Checkpoints capture pending placeholders and any returned minimal tool metadata.
Reconciliation: on rehydrate, server will attempt to re-resolve placeholders; if tool results changed, server emits a 'patch' frame describing a minimal delta to apply.
Atomicity: client SDK exposes a 'commit' API for marking subgraphs of structured output as immutable; committed subgraphs are safe to rely on after rehydration.
attachment_and_prefetch_model: Attachments are referenced by content-addressed ids (CID) or short object ids; checkpoints contain only these pointers.
Prefetch policy hints: server may include 'hotness' scores across checkpoints to guide clients which attachments to prefetch.
Graceful degradation: if attachment not available on resume, SDK shows placeholder UI and triggers background prefetch; partial structured output should still be usable.
telemetry_and_observability: Logs: checkpoint_id, client_sdk_version, device_context, server_fallback_reason for failed resumes
Tracing: attach trace-id to each checkpoint and rehydrate flow so we can correlate user-facing latency to server restores.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (experiments): ship SDK feature flag to internal beta apps; gather metrics on snapshot sizes and resume success (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (opt-in): expose to early customers behind a enable_dehydration flag; require SDK upgrade and collection of telemetry (4 weeks).
Phase 2 (gradual enable): enable default light checkpoints for mobile clients with opt-out; provide migration notes for tool authors (6–8 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): public docs, console controls for checkpointing frequency, and billing guidance for attachment prefetch bandwidth.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Checkpoints leak sensitive ephemeral data. Mitigation: default encryption at rest for persisted checkpoints and scrub sensitive fields by schema blacklists; enterprise option to disallow client-side persistence.
Risk: Tool replay causes side effects on rehydrate. Mitigation: require idempotency tokens and server-side verification; default to returning 'tool-state' not re-executing destructive ops.
Risk: Snapshot metadata size grows. Mitigation: cap checkpoint size and switch to pointer-only mode; server issues 'too-large' warnings and SDK reduces frequency.
open_questions: How do we sign and version checkpoint schemas so older SDKs can still rehydrate newer server-side summaries?
What is the canonical set of sensitive fields to redact in a checkpoint (PII, API keys, tokens)?
Should the server opportunistically compact a sequence of checkpoints into a single resumed snapshot and expose that compaction API to clients?
How to surface replay vs resume to end-users in applications with strict audit trails?
next_steps: Tech spike: implement a lightweight proto for checkpoint metadata and validate avg snapshot sizes on 3 production workloads (team: applied-ml + hosted-api runtime).
SDK: PR with the startStream/checkpoint/resume API stubs and an internal sample app demonstrating offline resume UX (owner: devexp).
Security review: define default redaction rules and enterprise controls for persisted checkpoints (owner: security-and-compliance).
Design: produce UX microcopy for placeholder states and rehydrate progress indicators (owner: product-hosted-api).
Metrics: add telemetry events for checkpoint lifecycle and wire them to the console for early customers.
